text:
Doris Day, 
the quintessential all-American girl, continues to be revered by her fans, while the media still celebrate her as an actress and singer with a legendary Hollywood "girl next door" image.

However, Doris Day's personal life, faced with steely resolve, was the very antithesis of how most fans perceived her super-stardom.  The studios promoted her in screen roles highlighting her wholesome, vivacious blonde personality. However, in hindsight, this concentration on her image belied her great acting and musical talents; a full retrospective appraisal of her career in recent years has brought her fans a fuller appreciation of her gifts.  Of her 39 films, Calamity Jane, Love Me or Leave Me and Pillow Talk remain popular favorites, and still run frequently on cable television.  Paralleling her success in big-screen entertainment, a series of excellent albums recorded between 1956 and 1968 expanded her popularity, and are as relevant today as when they were first released.

The Singer | The Actress | Notable Achievements | The Television Personality | Challenges & Honors | More Recently … | People Are Saying | Life & Legacy Video |
The Singer
Born Doris Mary Ann von Kappelhoff on April 3, 1922, in Cincinnati, Ohio, her parents came from German stock.  Her father, Frederick Wilhelm Von Kappelhoff, was a music teacher, choir master and church organist and loved classical music.  Her mother, Alma Sophia Welz, on the other hand, was an outgoing woman who enjoyed "hillbilly music."  Doris was the youngest of three: she had two brothers, Richard, who died before she was born, and Paul who was a few years older. She was named after silent movie actress Doris Kenyon, whom her mother admired. Growing up in the 1930s Doris was attracted to music and dance, eventually forming part of a dance duo which performed locally until a car she was riding in was struck by a train, crushing her right leg, a severe injury that curtailed her ambition to become a professional dancer.
However, while recovering, Doris gained a vocal education by listening to the radio, becoming a fan of the embryonic records of upcoming Ella Fitzgerald. Her mother encouraged her to take singing lessons. Alma took Doris to see vocal coach Grace Raine, who was so impressed with Doris' natural talent that she offered her three lessons for the price of one.  Doris credits Raine with impressing upon her the importance of delivering a lyric, and today Doris says that Raine had the greatest impact on her singing career.
At age 15, Doris began performing locally and while working with local bandleader Barney Rapp, she adopted the stage name "Day" after Rapp suggested "Kappelhoff" was too long and cumbersome for marquee appeal. After leaving Rapp, Doris worked with a number of other band leaders including Bob Crosby, and was eventually hired by Les Brown.  She had two stints with Brown's band, with marriage to trombonist Al Jorden, birth of her son Terry and subsequent divorce in between. Her 1945 hit "Sentimental Journey," co-written by Brown and recorded with his band, was made at the ideal time, as it reflected the thoughts of weary troops as they returned home from service in Europe and the Pacific.
"She was every bandleader's dream, a vocalist who had natural talent, a keen regard for the lyrics and an attractive appearance." - Les Brown
Following her second hit record with Brown, "My Dreams Are Getting Better All The Time," Doris went solo with a contract from Columbia Records in 1947.   Her radio work (with Bob Hope and later Frank Sinatra) lead to separation (and eventually divorce) from second husband George Weidler. Weidler could see that Doris was becoming a notable personality, and he did not want to be known as Mr. Doris Day. His request for a divorce came via letter while she was performing at the Little Club in New York.
The Actress

"I'll remember this to my grave.  We all walked into a room to see the screen tests.  The first screen test was Marion Hutton's. Then came Janis Paige [who ended up with a part in the film].  Then on the screen came Doris Day.  I can only tell you, the screen just exploded. There was absolutely no question.  A great star was born and the rest is history." - Sammy Cahn
Still despondent over her divorce, Doris reluctantly accepted an invitation to sing at a Hollywood party attended by songwriters Jule Styne and Sammy Cahn. She was asked to sing and gave a tearful, emotionally charged rendition of "Embraceable You." So impressed was Styne that he arranged for a screen test.  This lead to her first movie, Romance on the High Seas (1948), with director Michael Curtiz, who placed Doris under a personal contract for further films at Warner Brothers. Tea for Two (1950), Lullaby of Broadway (1951), On Moonlight Bay (1951), By the Light of the Silvery Moon (1953) and Calamity Jane (1953) were among the popular musicals that helped Doris sell hit records like "It's Magic" and "Secret Love." The occasional dramatic role, such as in the dark Storm Warning (1950) and musical melodrama Young Man with a Horn (1950), proved Doris had natural acting talent.

On a personal level, Doris married her agent, Marty Melcher, in 1951.  He subsequently handled her career as her producer and decided not to renew her contract with Warner Brothers after the completion of Young At Heart in 1954. As a freelance actress, Doris' range of roles increased. She made the bio-pic Love Me Or Leave Me, based on the life of ‘20s singer Ruth Etting, in 1955 for MGM; it was hailed as a triumph for both her singing and acting.  She followed this with Alfred Hitchcock's The Man Who Knew Too Much (1956), which teamed her with James Stewart and included location work in Morocco and London. On set, Doris asked Hitch why he wasn't giving her any direction.  His response was simple: "Because you are doing everything just right," he said.

Doris' recording of "Que Sera, Sera (Whatever Will Be, Will Be)" was used as an innocuous plot device in the film, and won an Oscar for Best Song. When Doris later recorded "Que Sera Sera" for Columbia, it became such a massive hit, it was henceforth perceived as her signature number.  Today, Doris casually admits to initially disliking the song.

Doris returned to Warner Brothers for the film version of Broadway hit The Pajama Game in 1957.  She was ideally cast as a feisty union shop-steward in a pajama factory, and the film included great songs that kept the action buoyant. Doris starred in comedies with Clark Gable, Jack Lemmon, Richard Widmark and David Niven. Then, in 1959, Doris paired with Rock Hudson in Pillow Talk for Universal.  This role gained her a Best Actress Oscar nomination and a Golden Globe Award and began a run of sophisticated romantic comedies. The onscreen chemistry between Doris and Hudson led to two more films, Lover Come Back and Send Me No Flowers. That Touch of Mink (1962) with Cary Grant lacked the same screen chemistry that was so apparent with Hudson, but the glow was back when she teamed up with James Garner in The Thrill of It All (1963) and Move Over Darling (1963). The dramatic Midnight Lace (1960) with Rex Harrison was an emotionally draining role for Doris. As for musicals, Jumbo gave Doris the lovely Rodgers & Hart score to sing, but the circus story based on a ‘30s Broadway spectacle was too old-fashioned to make any impression in 1962.
Doris was voted Top Box-Office Female Star for four straight years during the early ‘60s, and was among the Top 10 for 10 straight years.  Her record has never been matched, but fickle tastes eventually rejected such frothy fun for Hollywood's more explicit sex and darker themes. By mid-decade her box-office appeal had slipped a few notches, but Melcher continued to star Doris in light-weight fare with Move Over Darling and The Glass Bottom Boat (1966), the best of the bunch thanks to Doris' personable appeal. Ironically, her final movie, With Six You Get Egg-Roll (1968), gave an indication that roles nearer her actual age might be the way forward.

Notable Achievements
The title song from Move Over Darling gave Doris a major Top 20 hit in 1964. Produced and co-written by her son Terry, the song's success encouraged Doris to focus on more contemporary numbers.  But when her Columbia Records contract ended, a 1967 independent album project entitled The Love Album not only concluded her recording career but was ironically unissued for more than 27 years, with its belated 1994 UK issue preceding a 2006 U.S. release. It is widely agreed that when she recorded The Love Album she was at the peak of her vocal prowess, with many critics and fans considering this her finest album.  This fact is especially gratifying for Doris, since she personally selected the songs.
Despite numerous hit singles throughout her career, Doris' recording achievements are best celebrated by 16 superb concept albums.  Among these, Duet recorded in 1962 with the Andre Previn Trio, embodied all that is great about Doris' vocal style.  The album features minimal jazz accompaniment, which highlights her up-close-and-personal approach to the lyrics and melodic vocal strength. I Have Dreamed (1961) was dedicated to softly reflective numbers, and naturally displayed an intimate appeal, shot through with sensitivity. Cuttin' Capers (1959) proved to be a knock-out, up-and-at-‘em swinger that hit its mark with a mix of brilliantly orchestrated standards and newer numbers. The extended chart success of the Love Me or Leave Me soundtrack was joined by similar souvenirs from The Pajama Game and Billy Rose's Jumbo. Thankfully all these albums are still available, together with various compilations that feature her many singles.

But Doris wasn't done yet.  In 2011 at age 89, Doris became the oldest living recording artist to chart on UK's Top Ten with new material featured on her album, My Heart. Released through her Arwin Productions, the compilation contained previously unreleased material hand-picked by Doris, primarily recorded for her 1985-86 television series, Doris Day's Best Friends, along with four American Songbook favorites from Doris' vast catalog of recordings.  The album was dedicated to her son, Terry Melcher, who had passed away in 2004, and who produced and co-wrote some of the featured songs, including the title tune.  A particularly moving moment is Doris' spoken introduction of Terry singing "Happy Endings," a wistful song he had originally written for Doris to perform.  In the US, the album's surprising success landed its debut at #135 on the Billboard 200 chart, and Doris donated the proceeds to the Doris Day Animal Foundation.

"When I recorded for Columbia, I could usually do anything in one take...I would invariably want to use the first take because that would be the one that was spontaneous and fresh." - Doris Day

The Television Personality
The sudden death of Marty Melcher in 1968 was catalyst to Doris' discovering he and business partner Jerry Rosenthal had squandered her earnings, leaving her deeply in debt. Years were taken up suing Rosenthal in the courts, with a large civil judgment eventually awarding Doris over $26 million dollars.  After legal fees, she received only a fraction of that amount. Doris also discovered Melcher had committed her to a television sitcom series. Despite grave misgivings, and a dislike of television, the ultimate need to clear her debts convinced Doris to go ahead with The Doris Day Show, netting her a Golden Globe (1969) for Best Actress in a Television Series. With annual changes in formula, she successfully steered the series for five years (1968-1973) as co-executive producer with son Terry and grew to enjoy the work.  Her contract completed, she left the grueling schedule on her own terms. Additionally, two television specials, The Doris Mary Anne Kappelhoff Special (1971) and Doris Day Today (1975), gave Doris a chance to sing with friends Perry Como and John Denver as guests. A cable television series, Doris Day's Best Friends, during 1985-86 featured celebrity guest stars in primarily a talk-show format, with topics mainly dedicated to animal welfare.

Publication of her autobiography, Doris Day - Her Own Story, in 1976 was a surprisingly honest account, as related to A. E. Hotchner. The book revealed much of the painful trauma in her private life and three marriages, which had been masked by her sunny on-screen and recording image, and how her positivity enabled her to emerge a survivor. Television interviews ensured the book became a best seller.
Challenges & Honors

"I always felt that making a living wasn't the easiest thing in the world, and I decided I was going straight ahead and try to be as uncomplicated as possible. The important thing in life is just living and loving." - Doris Day

text:
Josh, the Puerto Rico comparison doesn't hold up.

Puerto Ricans have been US citizens since 1917. If one moves from San Juan to Orlando, they vote for president in the next election. 

Name the Palestinian in Nablus who can move to Tel Aviv and register to vote.

In Puerto Rico, the rule is about where you live, not who you are. An American born in Ohio who moves to San Juan loses the federal vote too. In the West Bank, a settler and a Palestinian can live on the same hill. One votes for the Knesset and the other doesn't. 

That rule is drawn around people, not around territory.

Puerto Ricans also aren't tried by uniformed military judges while their mainland neighbors get civilian courts. They elect their own governor and legislature, send a Resident Commissioner to Congress, and have voted in several referendums on their own status. 

Palestinians in Area C have no vote over the authority that issues their permits, controls their water, and demolishes their homes.

"They don't want citizenship"? It has never been offered. Israel annexed East Jerusalem in 1967 and gave the Palestinians there residency, not citizenship. 

When they apply, they mostly get turned down: from 2014 to 2016, about 4,000 applied and 84 were approved. Smotrich's 2017 "Decisive Plan" was explicit about it. 

Palestinians could stay without voting rights, leave, or fight.

"Only citizens can vote." Correct. And the state that decides who becomes a citizen is the same one that has ruled them for 59 years. 

That's my point.  The same one you can’t disprove.

So pick one. If it's Israel, the people living there are owed citizenship. If it's occupied, the ICJ ruling you skipped applies. "Judea and Samaria" is a way to claim the land without taking on the people who live on it.

text:
She paid for the groceries.

Walmart says the rest was hidden underneath the cart. 

At an Illinois Walmart, a woman shopping with her children went through self-checkout and paid for the food with EBT and a small debit payment.

But loss prevention said about $171 worth of clothing, shoes, paper towels, sippy cups and other merchandise never got scanned.

The paid groceries were on top.

The unpaid merchandise was underneath.

After she passed checkout, employees stopped her.

She said she had been distracted by the kids and offered to pay for anything that was missed.

Then Walmart checked the cameras.

Police were called, she was arrested on a retail-theft allegation, and Walmart told her she could no longer return to the store.

The groceries she had actually paid for were given to her boyfriend so the family could take them home.

Self-checkout may not have a cashier watching you…

but somebody usually is.

text:
Something strange appeared over Chicago’s O’Hare Airport in 2006.

And multiple airport workers said they saw it.

On November 7, United Airlines employees reported a silent, dark, disc-shaped object hovering near Gate C17 beneath the clouds.

Then, according to witnesses, it suddenly shot straight upward.

They said it punched through the cloud layer and left a strange circular opening behind.

The FAA suggested a weather phenomenon could have been responsible, but no formal investigation ever settled the mystery.

Then came another twist.

FAA recordings obtained later showed airport personnel really had been discussing reports of a “disc” over O’Hare.

Nearly 20 years later, there’s still no confirmed explanation.

Whatever hovered over O’Hare that day disappeared in seconds.

The mystery never did.

Anthropic's S-1 filing this week revealed a number that stops you in your tracks: $131.7 billion in cash and short-term investments on the balance sheet as of June 30, 2026 ($112.4B in cash plus $19.3B in marketable securities).

​Stack that liquidity pile against the Magnificent 7 and company filings:
• Alphabet: $242.5B
• Anthropic: $131.7B
• Amazon: $123.0B
• Meta: $90.3B
• Microsoft: $76.8B
• Nvidia: $62.5B
• Apple: $62.4B
• Tesla: $43.5B

​Before ringing the opening bell, a six-year-old AI lab sits on more balance-sheet cash than Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Apple, or Tesla (and across all non-bank U.S. companies, trails only Berkshire Hathaway and Alphabet).

​Now look inside the S-1 at what that $131.7 billion actually represents:

​First, it is capital raised, not accumulated free cash flow. Anthropic has raised $141.1 billion in private financing since 2021 to build that $131.7 billion reserve (even with H1 2026 revenue surging to $16.3 billion and operating cash flow turning positive at $3.9 billion).

​Second, that cash pile is already spoken for. The footnotes to the S-1 disclose $265.6 billion in fixed or minimum purchase commitments as of June 30 for cloud compute and infrastructure.

​Read what that means for capital allocation: Anthropic raised $141 billion from private markets, and virtually every dollar of that war chest is contractually destined to be transferred to hyperscale cloud providers, semiconductor foundries, networking suppliers, and power grids over the next decade.

​You do not need to chase a frothy IPO allocation to own the AI buildout. If you own the cash-flowing picks, shovels, and toll roads collecting that $265.6 billion in compute commitments, the capital raise is already flowing to your bottom line.

text:
Early this month, David Bateman, a prominent Utah entrepreneur and Republican political donor, sent an unusual email to his state’s business and political leaders, including Gov. Spencer Cox. The subject line? “Genocide.” The topic: Jews. But Bateman’s message was not about the Holocaust or about Jews being the victims of mass murder. Instead, he accused them of perpetrating it.
“I believe there is a sadistic effort underway to euthanize the American people,” Bateman wrote. “I believe the Jews are behind this. … I believe the pandemic and systematic extermination of billions of people will lead to an effort to consolidate all the countries in the world under a single flag with totalitarian rule. … No one is reporting on it, but the Hasidic Jews in the US instituted a law for their people that they are not to be vaccinated for any reason.” (No such law exists.)

Reached for comment by a bemused reporter, Bateman insisted that “some of my closest friends are Jews.” He resigned from his industry positions shortly afterward.
It’s tempting to write this off as the ridiculous ramblings of an Internet-poisoned tech magnate too rich to have ever been told “no” by those around him. On the surface, Bateman’s ham-handed harangue certainly looks like a fringe — even funny — story. But it’s not. That’s because the libel that Jews are committing genocide has exploded in popularity across anti-Jewish discourse. It crosses ideological lines and is increasingly expressed in polite company.
Five myths about antisemitism
Indeed, once you start looking, it’s hard to escape the fact that people just love accusing Jews of genocide. “The Jews will use the vaccine to change DNA making the person susceptible to designer viruses the Jews will create,” wrote one poster on the neo-Nazi forum Stormfront in December 2020. “This is one way the Jews will attempt to kill off the White Race.” That same month, the Anti-Defamation League reported that Ishmael Muhammad, a student minister in Louis Farrakhan’s Nation of Islam, had “referenced the ‘Synagogue of Satan’ (an antisemitic phrase used to refer to Jews) for allegedly promoting vaccines to sterilize Black people,” in a live sermon from the organization’s headquarters in Chicago. “Those of you who are really big supporters of the vaccination program, whether you realize it or not, you are a new Nazi,” intoned the antisemitic pastor Rick Wiles last month. “This is mass genocide.” (Wiles is best known for dubbing the impeachment of President Donald Trump a “Jew coup.”)

So far, so fringe. But the same cannot be said for the broader “white genocide” conspiracy theory, which posits that Jews are conspiring to wipe out the White race through the promotion of mass immigration, interracial marriage and other supposedly sinister social schemes. Fear of this farcical “great replacement” infamously inspired the neo-Nazi marchers in Charlottesville, who in 2017 chanted that “Jews will not replace us.” And it featured prominently in the social media feeds of Robert Bowers, the white supremacist who is accused of massacring 11 Jews at Pittsburgh’s Tree of Life synagogue in 2018.
Then, last year, the most popular political personality on American television took it mainstream. “The left and all the little gatekeepers on Twitter become literally hysterical if you use the term ‘replacement,’ if you suggest that the Democratic Party is trying to replace the current electorate, the voters now casting ballots, with new people, more obedient voters from the Third World,” Fox News’s Tucker Carlson declared in April. “But they become hysterical because that’s what’s happening actually.”
The Pittsburgh shooter didn’t hate ‘religion,’ he hated Jews. We should say so.
Of course, even if one were to accept the questionable premise of this accusation, adding new people to the United States does not remove the previous inhabitants. There is no “replacement” unfolding, other than in the fevered imagination of the country’s white nationalists. Carlson knows this. But he also knows the extremists in his audience and their preferred parlance. And so he chose to politely popularize the conspiratorial claims that had motivated the mass murder of American Jews. The message was received. “Tucker Carlson is talking about replacement theory; well, I knew it was going on way back then, way back in 1991,” exulted former KKK leader David Duke.

Many liberals strongly condemned Carlson’s remarks. And yet, false fulminations about Jews committing genocide have found a home in certain parts of the left as well. Last May, award-winning actor and outspoken Israel critic Mark Ruffalo apologized for publicly accusing the Jewish state of genocide. “It’s not accurate, it’s inflammatory, disrespectful & is being used to justify antisemitism here & abroad,” he wrote on Twitter. Israel occupies the Palestinian people, and the two have fought multiple wars. The Israeli military deserves scrutiny and criticism for every Palestinian civilian casualty. But occupation and discrimination are not genocide. In actuality, according to the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics, the Palestinian population in Israel, Gaza and the West Bank has increased about fourfold since Israel’s founding. By contrast, the Holocaust killed 2 out of 3 European Jews. Within Israel, where 20 percent of the population is Arab, the most popular male baby name for the past decade has been Muhammad.

Whatever one thinks of Israel, that’s obviously the opposite of genocide. Like most conspiracy theories, this one takes a kernel of truth — about Israel’s treatment of Palestinians — and inflates it into a crazed calumny. In other words, Ruffalo was right to back off his remarks. But the fact that this incendiary claim filtered all the way up to a Hollywood star, who initially felt comfortable repeating it in public, demonstrates how acceptable this libel is even in some putatively progressive circles.

Obviously, not all of these allegations are equivalent. Some are spread through ignorance, others through malice. But by now, it should be clear that people don’t make these accusations because they make sense. Rather, false charges of Jewish genocide continue to proliferate because they offer tantalizing rewards that make them irresistible to a certain brand of bigot.
First, they weaponize the greatest Jewish trauma against Jewish people. As the Marxist political theorist Norm Geras put it, “To say to Jews that what they are doing is just like what the Nazis did to them is to appeal to the comparison that is most hateful.” There is no better way to hurt someone than to fashion their most painful experience into a club with which to beat them. It’s not hard to imagine how turning the Holocaust on Jewish people, like turning slavery on Black people, provides a delicious transgressive thrill.

Second, casting Jews as the perpetrators of a new, fictitious Holocaust frees non-Jews from the obligation to learn the lessons of the actual Holocaust. “For thousands of years, for much of the world, part of the cultural patrimony enjoyed by all non-Jews — spiritual and secular, Church and Mosque, enlightenment and romantic, European and Middle Eastern — was the unquestionable right to stand superior over Jews,” the University of California at Berkeley’s David Schraub wrote in 2016. “It was that right which the Holocaust took away, or at least called into question: the unthinking faith of knowing you were the more enlightened one, the spiritually purer one, the more rational one, the dispenser of morality rather than the object of it.”
Anti-vaxxers are claiming centuries of Jewish suffering to look like martyrs
In a masterful maneuver of moral jujitsu, pinning genocide on the Jews allows the bigot to swipe the “Holocaust card” and play it against them. The victims are transformed into perpetrators, and their judgment is called into question. “Many people deeply resent the Jews for what Auschwitz took away from them — the easy knowledge that their vantage point was elevated over and superior to that of the Jews,” notes Schraub. “The desire to neuter the Holocaust is a desire to return to that old state of affairs.”

This ominous outcome is why it is a mistake to dismiss efforts to fabricate a Jewish genocide as merely marginal or inconsequential. Fundamentally, the impulse to hang the Holocaust on the Jews is an attempt to return humanity to where it was before the Holocaust — which enables such things to happen again.
After all, making the Jews guilty of genocide doesn’t just obviate non-Jewish guilt for permitting Jewish genocide. It also justifies the next Jewish genocide.

🧫 “82-YEAR-OLD MAN REPORTS ON BLADDER CANCER AFTER 6 MONTHS OF ANTIPARASITIC DRUGS.” WHAT DOES THE EVIDENCE SHOW?

An X post promotes an article about an 82-year-old man in California with neuroendocrine bladder cancer. Its headline names ivermectin, fenbendazole and mebendazole and describes a six-month testimonial.

For someone facing cancer, such stories can offer hope. But the screenshot shows a headline, not the clinical evidence needed to judge whether the drugs helped.

🔬 The diagnosis matters. Neuroendocrine bladder cancer is rare and can behave aggressively. Treatment depends on the tumor's pathology, stage, the patient's health and whether disease has spread. Depending on the case, doctors may consider platinum-based chemotherapy, surgery, radiation or other approaches.

The post does not show the man's pathology report, original cancer stage, treatment timeline, scans or details of any standard treatment he may have received. It also does not establish whether the cancer shrank, remained stable or progressed during those six months.

💊 The drugs matter, too. Ivermectin and mebendazole treat certain human parasitic infections. Researchers have investigated their possible anticancer activity, mainly in laboratory models. Those findings have not established either drug as an effective treatment for neuroendocrine bladder cancer.

Fenbendazole is a veterinary antiparasitic, not an approved human cancer medicine. Human self-use has been associated with liver injury. Combining three drugs does not prove benefit or establish that the combination is safe.

📋 What would make this report meaningful? Verified imaging before and after treatment, pathology findings, a complete list of concurrent therapies, adverse-event reporting and independent medical review. Even then, a single case could generate a research hypothesis, not prove a cure.

Patients deserve legitimate treatment options, including appropriate clinical trials. A testimonial can be a starting point for questions, but it should never be mistaken for a validated cancer protocol.

All righty then.  This little series started with a look at Federalist #10 and how that document laid out a plan of action for the high-and-mighty to use the variety of factions across multiple jurisdictions to stop the formation of ‘majority factions’ dangerous to the ruling classes.

Put in simple terms, one upper crust criminal might snicker to another.  ‘We’ll make sure that their interests are very divided, so they can’t take our stuff!’  With very few exceptions, this scheme has worked like a toxic charm in the United States against people power’s ascendancy.

Many of the posts in this sequence will feature, as did the initial one, excerpts from an essay that This Humble Correspondent produced roughly fifteen years ago.  That piece’s title is evocative for our purposes: Undermining Majority ‘Factions:’ Federalist Paper #10 & the Evisceration of Popular Power in America.

My previous X installment ended with this advisory.  “In essence, the message is this.  The design of United States’ political machinery makes elections a façade, such that they appear to proffer, but cannot deliver, democracy.  

People power will never come to pass as a result of voting, even as the ballot does represent, at least, a small aspect of the possibility for democracy actually to happen at some point soon, for the first time in U.S. history.”

Today, and on other occasions upcoming, we will examine something that also touches near the heart of how electoral matters truly operate here in the ‘home of the brave,’ though this new factor is altogether different from my older essay’s line of reasoning.  It concerns the most potentially revolutionary campaign in American history.

As the PBS offering above documents, in 1934, Upton Sinclair—an avowed, decades-long radical—campaigned to a landslide victory in the California Democratic Party primary.  Moreover, his efforts built a gigantic grassroots following.

Not only was he not ever a regular follower of the Democrats, he was a confirmed socialist who out of hand refused to condemn, and in many ways openly admired, the young Soviet Union’s experiments in communism.  Thus, his victory in one of the country’s most important states—the heart of Hollywood and much more—would have been a disaster without parallel in the American experience.

Much of the rest of today’s episode excerpts and considers pieces of the famous author’s book about this experience.  I, Candidate For Governor, And How I Got Licked highlights Sinclair’s good humored consideration of the treachery, slander, and double-dealing that destroyed this big opportunity to attempt social change through the ballot box.

Chapter V deals with how a man like Sinclair came so close to such an achievement, which would have been many times more threatening even than the ‘New Deal’ itself, which so upset the ruling potentates that the Liberty League itself sought a coup against Roosevelt.  

After introducing the context of his work—a million Californians unemployed, an equal number starving, desperation in the land—he outlines how his EPIC End Poverty In California plan inaugurated a fresh approach to electoral contests.

“To the audiences I said, over and over again: ‘There is only one thing you can do for me, which is to vindicate the faith in the people which I have held to all my life.’  And they did that; from that point of view it was a magnificent triumph, through the whole year.

The people awakened; they studied and thought about their problems, they took charge of their own job.  They formed nearly two thousand clubs; they opened and financed several hundred headquarters; they paid for and circulated nearly half a million booklets and ten or fifteen million newspapers; they organized thousands of meetings; they swept the Democratic primaries by the biggest vote ever polled, and ten weeks later they doubled that vote.  

And if anyone thinks they are through yet, he has something to learn about politics in the State of California!”

Chapter VI details the way that ‘politics as usual’ works so as to inhibit if not outright destroy true popular empowerment.  The incessant, both unrelenting and essential, need was for more money to conduct the necessary ‘campaigning.’  Obtaining this lifeblood cashola without lethal compromise might rarely if ever appear possible, if Upton’s instructive experience, perhaps dispositive, proves persuasive.

“There was money to be had for our campaign, but unfortunately always money that we could not take.  As soon as it became evident that we had a real movement, we began to have visits from well-dressed, smooth-spoken persons familiar with politics, who offered us the solution to all our problems.

The first was a representative of a group of men who conducted a gambling game, and at that time were taking sixty-five thousand dollars a day from the people of Los Angeles.  All these people wanted to know was that if I was elected Governor I would let them alone. 
 
On that basis I could have ‘anything within reason.’  I never found out how much that was, because I told the gentleman that we were not making political promises, except those in our program.”

This pattern seemed unending and unavoidable.  Again and again, the whiff of corruption and its predilection for ‘favors’ fouled the air.

“All through the campaign we struggled with a load of debt, and had these fortunes dangling before our eyes.  One of our San Francisco workers, a manufacturer ruined by the depression and living by the kindness of his son, received a visit from a representative of the gamblers of San Francisco, who offered us sixteen thousand dollars per month, not merely during the period of the campaign but during the four years of my incumbency.  

That worked out at close to nine hundred thousand dollars.  Later on when I saw our opponents’ pouring out unlimited treasure I was able to guess where it had come from.”

He offers up the story of a ‘promising young volunteer’ who kept running into roadblocks over lack of currency.  His original idealism descended into the trough of money-grubbing opportunism.

“‘Upton, we gotta have the dough!’ he cried.  It was not the language they had taught him at the university, but the language of politics which he had taken up.  ‘We gotta have the dough, I tell you.  You can't win any election without dough.’

‘But where can we get it?’ I asked.”  And the youngster tried to set the hook and reel in the idealistic candidate to agree with his proposition.

A ‘friend’ of the callow lad wanted to be Fish-&-Game Commissioner.  He ‘just likes to fish and hunt’ the man protested to the charge that such favoritism would tar the campaign with a wicked brush.  Sinclair then continues, relating what happened during one of the candidate’s own outings with rod-and-reel.

“‘There do not seem to be many fish here.’  My friend replied that it was the commercial fishing that had ruined these fishing grounds.  I asked if there were not laws on the subject, and my friend said: ‘Yes, but you see the commercial fisheries invite Jimmy Rolph down and give him a banquet once a year, and then they name the fish and game commissioners, and can do what they please.’”

From Chapter VII, dealing with success and its defamatory results, comes the following. “We were not permitted to sell literature in school-house meetings—it is one of the devices by which the reactionaries keep the people from getting new ideas.  

But there was no way to keep people from buying books on the sidewalk outside, nor to keep me from telling them that the books were on sale outside.”

To stop the mass movement that Sinclair was building—speaking literally to millions of Californians who came to mass meetings during the Democratic primary—“‘Lie Factories’” began an assembly line of falsehoods about Sinclair, starting with an L.A.Times hit piece in which not a single accusation proved accurate.  McClatchy's mentioned media interests were another link in monopoly's chain.

“Mr. McClatchy resents the statement that he got(this slander)from the Times,’ and claims the dubious honor of having published it first.  All right, Mr. McClatchy!  You think you have done your full duty because you allowed me to deny the slanders in your columns—but with no retraction or apology from you.

What I ask is, why, before publishing grave charges against a man's honor, not give the man a chance to say whether there is any basis of fact in them?  The answer is, because you wanted to discredit the man, and you didn't care what means you used.”

Finally, for the moment, readers can read and think about a primary driver of California’s politicos in their condemnation of Sinclair, which shows up especially in Chapters X and XII.  This particular slant on slander involved American plutocrats’ only true religion, which ever amounts to anticommunism.

One incident would be hilarious were it not such a tragic epitome of ‘land of the free’ electioneering.  A bunch of actual Reds showed up at the Sinclair-for-Governor headquarters, outraged that he had dared to suggest that these true revolutionary proletarians had endorsed him, whom they had long and vociferously pilloried.

Apparently, a widely posted flyer had appeared that claimed a fictitious organization, whose name approximated a real group, had joined the radical bandwagon.  The posted broadsheet showed an image of the candidate next to the hammer-and-sickle and asserted in its text that Sinclair and the commies had made common cause.

“The circulars had appeared simultaneously all over Southern California and in the Bay cities.  Boys had received armfuls to distribute, and were promised fifty cents each for the service—though many of them never got the money.  

There was no such organization as the ‘Young People's Communist League of Los Angeles.’  There is a ‘Young People's Socialist League’ and a ‘Young Communist League,’ but neither had anything to do with this matter.’”

Later, the choice of California’s democrats lamented.  “Having been a Socialist for thirty-two years...I really thought I was safe from being called a Communist.  I have been tireless in my insistence upon majority consent, and in my rejection of every suggestion of violence and dictatorship in bringing about social change.  

Early in the campaign, the Western Worker, organ of the Communist Party on the Pacific Coast, described the EPIC plan as ‘one more addled egg from the blue buzzard's nest.’”

Oh my!  These distortions, partial truths, and generally plain and simple lies suffused the opposition to any hint of Ending Poverty In California.  Upton often wrote for the Socialist magazine The Masses, which his opponents purposefully conflated with the CP’s weekly, The New Masses.  Long gone organizational affiliations with early ‘commie front groups’ somehow now demonstrated his being an “agent of Moscow.”

One especially egregious defamation concerned a reference in a five year old pamphlet that Upton had authored about resorting to violence, which Mr. Sinclair pacifically insisted was unnecessary if common citizen availed themselves of legal methods.  “I was pointing out to my readers what had happened in American history.

Abraham Lincoln had fought the slave power, using constitutional means; he had carried an election, and left it to the slave power to attempt to revolt against the people's verdict; so he had kept the moral forces of America on his side. ...I was pleading with American workingmen to display the same wisdom in obtaining their rights.

I was appealing to the people of California to display that same wisdom—and my fellow-Democrat was lying about what I had written!”  Welcome to America’s realpolitik, about which further lessons follow in this ‘midterm season.’

text:
A Decision Is Not the Same as the Capability to Act

Two households receive the same energy-price shock and make the same rational response: they cut consumption. One absorbs it — savings buffer it, an efficient home limits it, remote work removes its worst edge. The other cannot: savings deplete, retraining is deferred, work ends early. Identical behaviour. Different economy.

Economics sees the decision very well. It is largely blind to the structural conditions that determined which decisions were available in the first place.

Today The Global Structure Network publishes the expanded institutional edition of The Household Affordability Frontier. It defines the structural threshold at which the combined financial, temporal, physical and participation costs of household life begin to restrict the capacity to accumulate and deploy productive capability — and connects three domains usually examined separately: household structural conditions, monetary transmission and heterogeneous-agent dynamics, and the allocation of long-duration capital.

For central banks, institutional investors, infrastructure capital and economic strategy teams, the practical question is straightforward: which structural costs are currently preventing existing capability from becoming productive capacity, and which forms of investment can measurably expand the residual space in which households can adapt?

The framework does not claim empirical superiority over existing approaches. It is offered as a proposed analytical architecture, not a finished model — with explicit measurement requirements, testable hypotheses and clear falsification conditions published in full. If threshold position and duration below it carry no predictive power beyond income and balance sheets, the framework fails.

What is stated here can be tested — by design.

text:
Australia has long had a really egalitarian culture with a firm anti-authoritarian streak, and a dislike of showy, pretentious speech, or self aggrandisement of any kind. Americans tend to have a different aesthetic. 
The first de-facto Australian national anthem "Waltzing Matilda"  was literally about a homeless guy who steals a sheep then commits suicide to avoid arrest.  This is not a hero-worshipping culture. 

A significant minority of our foundation stock was Irish, and we had Irish political prisoners incarcerated here to get them out of the UK from early Colonial times. This combined readily with an ex-convict minority who had a deep seated mistrust of authority , exemplified by characters like Ned Kelly. 
But a more general cynicism  towards the aristocratic, British part of Ausralian society that included many leading business figures and large institutional concerns remained, and the later Socialist mistrust of Elites transferred easily to "bosses" of any sort. 
Australia's organised labour movements and Fabianism have greatly influenced Australian culture and political aesthetics, if not always  actual policy; even as many of the  Australian business leaders who emerged post-War were entirely self-made, including literal refugees like the Smorgon family who built steel mills and the Meyers who built the leading department stores - there remained a strong feeling against the "Big End of Town" more generally. As British capital declined, American companies came to take their place, and certainly inherited some of that left-wing antipathy. 

Australia has fought for Britain in every conflict from the Boer War until Korea, entering years before the US in both world wars and losing staggering numbers of men relative to population. The soldiers were volunteers in most cases and like most Commonwealth troops had positively miserable wages and rough conditions compared to the Americans . 

Particularly in WW2 there was a lot of resentlent from Australian troops returning home after many years of war to find Americans who earned five times their salaries and had access to then-unobtainable consumer products fron US stores like stockings and chocolate- making free with the Aussies' wives and girlfriends while on leave in Australian port cities. There were significant brawls over this between large groups of soldiers on leave at times. 

"Overpaid, oversexed and over here" was the joke about this time.

I would argue though that none of this amounts to actual hatred in most cases. Australia does have an extremely sharp sense of humour that is never happier than when cutting down "tall poppies". Americans are therefore seen as the legitimate butt of jokes, and the unfortunate sneering sort of humour that Social Studdies teachers encourage their little sheep to engage in. But this is not hatred. 

Labor policies, have rejected revolutionary forms of socialism, but keep Socialist policy objectives; these are sought via  Government spending, rather than radical change. The ideas of Keynesian Stim and "MMT" offered them a black checkbook post 2007 and the resulting public sector expansion created enormous bureaucratic structures, that employ nearly one-fifth of the population; another one-third are on some sort of pension or support. This is reflected in a widespread ambivalence towards business from large portions of the population. State schooling, with strong teachers' unions, make sure that these political aesthetics are transferred to the young. 

In spite of all this, I think actual hate towards Americans is rare. Quite scathing humour is common, but Aussies don't spare each other from that either so it shouldn't be taken too personally. 

Australia does have a strong Conservative backbone as well; Australia's conservatives appreciate US very much indeed and absolutely adore it when they travel there. In fairness most of the lefties ("Pinkos" in Aussie slang, they don't escape a nickname either) love it too if they go.

text:
The Night the Otherworld Opened — The Adventure of Nera

In medieval Irish literature, Samhain was a time when the ordinary world and the Otherworld could meet.

On Samhain Eve, King Ailill and Queen Medb hold a feast at their royal stronghold of Ráth Cruachan in Connacht.

Two captives have been hanged outside, and Ailill offers a reward to anyone brave enough to approach them and fasten a twig around the foot of one of the hanged men. One by one, the men venture into the darkness, but none succeeds.

Then Nera steps forward.

As he approaches the gallows, one of the dead men speaks to him and asks to be carried on his back to find a drink. Nera takes him to three houses, encountering strange and terrifying obstacles along the way, before returning him to the gallows.

When he finally returns to Cruachan, he sees a vision of the royal stronghold in ruins, its people apparently slain.

He follows a mysterious host into a cave and finds himself in the Otherworld.

There he discovers a strange kingdom where time passes differently. After what seems to him like three days and three nights, a woman of the Otherworld reveals that the destruction of Cruachan was a vision of an attack yet to come. She sends him back to warn his people, though in their world the feast has barely progressed.

As proof of his journey, he brings back the fruits of summer: wild garlic, primrose and golden fern.

The tale concludes with the extraordinary fate of Nera, who remains in the Otherworld until Doomsday.

The PlayStation 5 (PS5) is Sony's current generation of home video game consoles, available in standard (disc) and Digital Editions, as well as a more powerful Pro model released in November 2024. The original launch models have been replaced by slimmer hardware revisions.

Immersive Experience: Both models offer breathtaking 4K visuals (up to 120fps on compatible games) and the Tempest Engine for hardware-accelerated 3D Audio effects.

DualSense Controller: Features haptic feedback (realistic physical sensations) and adaptive triggers (dynamic resistance) for deeper immersion.

Ultra-High Speed SSD: A custom solid-state drive allows for lightning-fast loading times, enabling game developers to design vast worlds with near-instant data streaming.

Backward Compatibility: The PS5 is compatible with the vast majority of PlayStation 4 games, many of which benefit from faster and smoother frame rates with Game Boost technology.

PS5 Pro Enhancements: The Pro model features a faster GPU (about 45% faster), improved ray tracing, and AI-driven upscaling technology (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution or PSSR).

Immersive Experience: Both models offer breathtaking 4K visuals (up to 120fps on compatible games) and the Tempest Engine for hardware-accelerated 3D Audio effects.

DualSense Controller: Features haptic feedback (realistic physical sensations) and adaptive triggers (dynamic resistance) for deeper immersion.

Ultra-High Speed SSD: A custom solid-state drive allows for lightning-fast loading times, enabling game developers to design vast worlds with near-instant data streaming.

Backward Compatibility: The PS5 is compatible with the vast majority of PlayStation 4 games, many of which benefit from faster and smoother frame rates with Game Boost technology.

PS5 Pro Enhancements: The Pro model features a faster GPU (about 45% faster), improved ray tracing, and AI-driven upscaling technology (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution or PSSR).

text:
Russia is extending its war into waters around NATO countries. Failure to deter attacks on commercial shipping risks further escalation.

Throughout October 2026, drones struck merchant vessels near Romania and Bulgaria. Ships sank, leaving seafarers dead or missing. Most attacks occurred in exclusive economic zones, distinct from sovereign territorial waters. NATO also reported vessels targeted inside Romanian territorial waters on 14–15 October. A NATO military source told Reuters that Russian drones caused fires aboard two tankers, while Ambrey assessed Russian responsibility for several other attacks as highly likely. Individual incidents remain under investigation, but the pattern suggests an expanding campaign against commercial navigation.

Russia has repeatedly tested NATO’s boundaries. Its drones have violated Romanian airspace, leaving debris on Romanian territory. In October, Romanian fighter jets reportedly shot down two Russian drones over territorial waters. Earlier incidents require distinction: the drone that exploded in Constanța in June was acknowledged as Ukrainian, with Kyiv blaming Russian electronic interference. An explosive-laden maritime drone destroyed near Neptun Deep in August presented another threat, without establishing Russian responsibility. Neither qualification diminishes the evidence linking Russia to October’s attacks.

NATO’s deployments have not prevented attacks. On 28 October, naval drones struck the Liberian-flagged Contship Jet in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone while it sailed from Haifa to Constanța. A French maritime patrol aircraft had warned of an attack, but Bulgarian authorities could not prevent it. The ship sank; all 18 crew members were rescued. Its voyage illustrates why this cannot be treated simply as a problem for vessels carrying Ukrainian exports. Warning without protection leaves crews exposed.

The Alliance has announced additional patrol aircraft, radars, drones, intelligence personnel and explosives specialists. These should improve surveillance and attribution. Yet detecting a drone and stopping it are different tasks. No dedicated NATO shipping-protection mission comparable to its Baltic deployment has been publicly announced. Will these capabilities provide protection, or merely better documentation after ships have been hit?

The Baltic offers a comparison. Following damage to undersea infrastructure, NATO launched Baltic Sentry in January 2025, combining frigates, patrol aircraft, naval drones and national surveillance systems. Coastal states have investigated suspicious vessels and, where justified, boarded, detained or impounded them. Such action requires evidence and lawful grounds; association with Russia’s shadow fleet alone does not establish responsibility for sabotage. Nevertheless, surveillance backed by credible enforcement increases the risks for those contemplating attacks.

Black Sea security rests on a different framework. Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye established MCM Black Sea to counter naval mines, expanding its mandate in July 2026 to protect critical undersea infrastructure. This does not automatically protect moving ships against drones. The Montreux Convention restricts warship access and deployments, particularly for countries without a Black Sea coastline. A stronger response must accommodate those constraints, with the three coastal NATO members central to its implementation.

Persistent threats require coordinated protection. Surveillance must support interception, emergency assistance and investigation. Where Russian responsibility is established, attacks must carry tangible consequences. Moscow should not conclude that shipping near NATO’s shores offers an expanding field of operations at tolerable cost. Deterrence is measured by the attacks it prevents. Civilian crews should not discover its shortcomings one sinking at a time.

Weakness Invites Aggression!

text:
BLIMEY: 🏗️ This North Devon house needed a second house to help fund it—then the building site wrecked the rescue plan.

In 2014, music businessman Edward Short borrowed £500,000 to build a smaller home beside the lighthouse-style family house he wanted to create on the North Devon coast.

The smaller house, called The Eye, was meant to unlock the money for the big one.

Eventually, the unfinished big one stopped The Eye fetching the price he needed.

That is the particularly painful part of Chesil Cliff House: the escape route depended on the very project it was supposed to rescue.

Edward and his wife Hazel had bought a 1950s house on the clifftop in 2008, with two rocky coves below and room to bring up their two daughters.

They already had the extraordinary setting.

What they wanted was a house that matched it.

Architect Alan Phillips designed a white coastal mansion with a four-storey tower, huge windows and an infinity pool facing the sea.

At the top of the tower would be a glass-walled storm room, somewhere to watch the weather roll in.

Even getting from the road to the front door required a driveway built like a bridge.

This was a new house shaped like a lighthouse, rather than an old lighthouse being converted.

And the cliff made building it far more involved than clearing a plot and pouring some foundations.

The design used 25 deep steel-and-concrete piles to anchor the house to the slate bedrock.

Planning permission arrived in 2010, but the money did not follow as hoped.

During the economic downturn in 2012, the bank refused the £1.8 million loan Edward needed.

His earnings from the music business were falling too, as the CD sales that had supported his income disappeared.

So he tried to make the land provide the answer.

Borrowing £500,000 from a hedge fund allowed him to build The Eye, a separate three-bedroom home at the edge of the plot.

He could then borrow against that property to help pay for the lighthouse house.

The arrangement helped him secure £2.5 million from private investors, with building costs and professional fees already pushing the required borrowing higher.

There were now two houses in the plan, and the smaller one had a financial job to do before the larger one was finished.

In 2016, the family moved into rented accommodation and work on the main house got under way.

The rock proved exceptionally hard.

Even specialist mining equipment could not stop the foundations and piles taking an extra six months, eating through the money set aside for unexpected costs.

The bridge-like driveway became another expensive problem.

Edward then needed to sell The Eye to help fill the growing hole in the budget.

But a buyer paying a premium for a coastal home would have a hazardous building site next door.

The Eye could not command the price Edward needed while its neighbour remained unfinished.

By 2018, work had stopped and Edward was almost £4 million in debt.

The family home had been demolished, its replacement was a steel-and-concrete shell, and the smaller house had failed to release enough money to finish it.

Edward and Hazel separated under the strain.

He later accepted that his ambition had contributed to the breakdown of their marriage.

Finishing the house still required another round of borrowing.

A broker introduced Edward to a specialist property lender, and agreeing the new terms took two years.

When work restarted in April 2020, simply getting the abandoned site ready again cost £200,000.

Damaged windows needed attention, while the steelwork had to be scrubbed, resealed and repainted.

That money bought repairs to what was already there before the unfinished house could move forward.

The completed building finally delivered the sweeping glass, white tower and sea-facing pool that had made the original plan so tempting.

But Edward's task had changed from creating somewhere for his family to live to completing something he could sell.

In summer 2022, Chesil Cliff House and The Eye went on the market together for £10 million.

That was the asking price for both properties, not money Edward had received.

A potential sale fell through, and the homes were later offered separately at £7.5 million for the main house and £2.5 million for The Eye.

The main house subsequently returned to the market through Savills on behalf of joint receivers, the people appointed to handle the property for the lenders, with an asking price of £5.25 million.

By August 2025, Edward confirmed that the house had sold and described it as the closure of a long chapter.

The grand house was finished, but its owner had spent years getting it ready for somebody else.

text:
Stormy Daniels says she spanked Donald Trump with a Forbes magazine and slept with him while his wife was home with their 4-month-old son. Then a stranger threatened her baby. Then she got $130,000 to shut up. That money made Trump the first US president convicted of a felony.

It started in July 2006 at a celebrity golf tournament in Lake Tahoe. She was a 27-year-old adult film star working the event, he was a 60-year-old reality TV host with a wife at home and a four-month-old son. She says he invited her to dinner in his hotel suite, where she swatted him with a rolled-up copy of Forbes with his face on the cover, and they slept together that night. Trump has always denied it ever happened.

For five years she barely told anyone. Then in 2011 a tabloid called In Touch got hold of the story and she sat down with them for an interview. It never ran. Trump's lawyer Michael Cohen threatened to sue and the magazine shelved it. A few weeks later she was getting her daughter out of the car at a gym in Las Vegas when a stranger came up behind her and delivered the message. She says she was so scared she kept it to herself for years.

In October 2016 the story came back. Trump was days away from winning the presidency and Cohen wired $130,000 through a shell company he set up in Delaware. She signed an NDA under a fake name, Peggy Peterson. Trump was listed as David Dennison. When the Wall Street Journal broke the story in 2018, she signed two statements denying the affair. She later said she was pressured into signing both of them.

She says she had turned down far bigger offers over the years to tell the story. Then in March 2018 she went on 60 Minutes and told it for free. 22 million people watched. Cohen pleaded guilty, went to federal prison and turned on his former boss.

In May 2024 a New York jury found Trump guilty on all 34 counts of falsifying business records connected to the payment. He became the first former president convicted of a felony and still won the election that November. Stormy lost her defamation case against him and was ordered to pay his legal fees, which ran into hundreds of thousands of dollars.

She took $130,000 to stay quiet. Talking cost her more than the money ever paid.

Do you believe Stormy Daniels, or do you think she made the whole thing up?

text:
In Oxford, the federal case against a father and son accused of selling kratom-related drugs at a vape shop tied to the deaths of two Ole Miss students has taken its next step.

Court documents filed October 26 show Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, waived his arraignment in Oxford and pleaded not guilty to all charges against him in the indictment. He faces a felony charge of possession of a controlled substance with intent to distribute, alongside his co-defendant and father, Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51. When the Clarion Ledger published its report, no plea for the father had yet been entered in court records.

The son is out on bond pending trial — a $20,000 unsecured bond, with a curfew and location monitoring. His father remains in federal custody as he awaits trial.

The two men were arrested in September. According to the Clarion Ledger's reporting on the criminal complaint, investigators traced purchases made by two Ole Miss students who died on September 21 back to local shops — among them Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store on Heritage Drive in Oxford, where the Moslehs worked. Agents say a confidential informant bought kratom-based pills at the store on September 24, and that the clerk warned him to be careful with them because people were dying from them. A search of the business turned up more than 500 units of synthetic kratom, THC cartridges, gummies, and other suspected narcotics. Kratom is banned in both the city of Oxford and Lafayette County.

These charges are allegations the government must prove in court, and a not-guilty plea begins that testing. But no verdict can give two families back their sons. Parents, talk with your children about what is sold in gas stations and vape shops near campus — products marketed in bright packages, with narcotic-like effects, can kill.

THE GOOD NEWS: "Give justice to the weak and the fatherless; maintain the right of the afflicted and the destitute. Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked" (Psalm 82:3-4).

That is God's own heart: justice for the afflicted, and rescue for the vulnerable from the hand of the wicked. Pray for the two families grieving in the Ole Miss community, for truth in that Oxford courtroom, and for every student being offered a pill that promises a high and delivers a grave.

Come Alive in Christ. Grace to all.

text:
THE WORD OF THE LORD - GOSPEL YEAR A : ALL SAINTS' DAY https://t.co/yISSGBcw4t 
HOLY FATHER LEO XIV - ...It is the task of education to offer this Gentle Light to those who might otherwise remain imprisoned by the particularly insidious shadows of pessimism and fear. For this reason I would like to say to you: let us disarm the false reasons for resignation and impotence, and let us circulate in the contemporary world the great reasons for hope. Let us contemplate and point to constellations that transmit light and direction in this present darkened by so many injustices and uncertainties. Therefore I encourage you to make schools, universities and every educational institution, even informal and street-level ones, the thresholds of a civilization of dialogue and peace. Through your lives, let us see that "great multitude" of which the Book of Revelation speaks to us in today's liturgy, "which no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people and language" and who "stood before the Lamb" (7:9).

In the biblical text, an elder, observing the crowd, asks: "Who are these, and where do they come from?" (Rev 7:13). In this regard, even in the educational sphere, the Christian gaze rests on "those who have come out of the great tribulation" (v. 14) and recognizes in them the faces of so many brothers and sisters of every language and culture, who have entered into full life through Jesus' narrow door. And so, once again, we must ask ourselves: "Are not the less gifted human beings? Do not the weak have the same dignity as us? Are those born with fewer opportunities less worthy as human beings, limited only to surviving? The value of our societies depends on our answers to these questions, and our future depends on them as well" (Dilexi te, 95). And we add: the evangelical quality of our education also depends on this answer.

Among the enduring legacies of Saint John Henry are, in this sense, some very significant contributions to the theory and practice of education. "God," he wrote, "created me to render him a specific service. He entrusted me with a task he has not entrusted to others. I have a mission: perhaps I will not know it in this life, but it will be revealed to me in the next" (Meditations D. III, I, 2). In these words, we find beautifully expressed the mystery of the dignity of every human person and also that of the variety of gifts distributed by God.

Life is illuminated not because we are rich or beautiful or powerful. It is illuminated when we discover this truth within ourselves: I am called by God, I have a vocation, I have a mission, my life serves something greater than myself! Every single creature has a role to play. The contribution each person has to offer is of unique value, and the task of educational communities is to encourage and enhance that contribution. Let us not forget: at the center of educational programs must be not abstract individuals, but real people, especially those who appear to be underperforming, according to the parameters of an economy that excludes and kills. We are called to form people so that they may shine like stars in their full dignity.

We can therefore say that education, from a Christian perspective, helps everyone become saints. Nothing less. Pope Benedict XVI, on the occasion of his Apostolic Visit to Great Britain in September 2010, during which he beatified John Henry Newman, invited young people to become saints, with these words: "What God desires more than anything else for each of you is that you become saints. He loves you far more than you can imagine and wants the best for you." [2] This is the universal call to holiness that the Second Vatican Council made an essential part of its message (LG V). And holiness is proposed to everyone, without exception, as a personal and communal path traced by the Beatitudes.

I pray that Catholic education will help each person to discover his or her own call to holiness. St. Augustine once said that we are fellow students who have one Master, whose school is on earth and whose chair is in heaven.  1 November 2025
